predecessors.name: Sultanate of Malacca
predecessors.text: Malacca town: the fortress (Fortaleza) and the suburbs of Upe (Tranqueira), Hilir and Sabba, the only land the page describes

successors.name: Dutch Malacca
successors.text: Malacca town: the fortress (Fortaleza) and the suburbs of Upe (Tranqueira), Hilir and Sabba, the only land the page describes

ledger.x: January 1641: Portuguese Malacca ends with the fall of the city; Dutch Malacca follows.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Malacca
wars.outcome: The city fell on 24 August 1511 and Mahmud Shah fled; the Portuguese built a fortress and held the city for 130 years.

wars.name: Javanese and Johor attacks on Malacca
wars.outcome: Failed: Sultan Mahmud with Demak naval support (1511), a second Demak campaign (1521), and in 1550 Johor's request to Java brought Ratu Kalinyamat's '4,000 soldiers aboard 40 ships'.

wars.name: Aceh attacks on Malacca
wars.outcome: Failed: 1568 (Aceh), 1573-1575 (Aceh and Jepara together, 'largely from poor coordination') and 1629 (Iskandar Muda with several hundred ships; Portuguese sources say about 19,000 men were lost).

wars.name: Dutch sieges and capture of Malacca
wars.outcome: The Dutch siege of 1606 ended in a rout at the Battle of Cape Rachado and 'rallied the forces of the Sultanate of Johor into an alliance with the Dutch'; the Dutch attacked again in 1616 and, with Johor and Aceh, captured the city in January 1641.

certainty.note: The page describes a fortress city and its suburbs and no boundary; the three-cell outline is a city, not a frontier.
